new_cases.claim_text: Brigatinib was approved in May 2016 for ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC patients who progressed on or are resistant to crizotinib.
Brigatinib was approved in May 2016 and is now the universally preferred first-line cure for all NSCLC patients.
Brigatinib causes significant weight gain as its most common side effect.
Brigatinib was approved by the FDA in May 2019 for ALK-positive NSCLC.
A retrospective cohort study using Optum's Clinformatics database (2016-2024) compared first-line ALK TKIs in ALK-positive NSCLC patients, measuring time-to-next-treatment and overall survival.
The Optum retrospective study found brigatinib reduced mortality by exactly 50% compared to crizotinib.
Brigatinib is dosed at 90 mg orally once daily for the first 7 days, then increased to 180 mg once daily if tolerated.
Brigatinib is administered at a fixed dose of 300 mg once daily from treatment initiation.
The ALTA-1L trial is a phase III study comparing brigatinib with crizotinib in ALK-inhibitor-naive, ALK-positive NSCLC patients.
